title: Choose the visual world - bolder hand
question: You asked for bolder. All previous directions are eliminated. The dice lead with the data field; the concourse board beat it on both axes.

options.label: The City as Data Field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda's Datamatics - pure signal installations
options.thesis: Every report is a column of pure signal; the city renders as black-and-white data until something changes - then the field inverts.
options.viewport: A full-height field of vertical bars - one column per issue - with dense monospace margins; selecting a report pulls its numbers into focus while the rest faints to pattern.

raised.raise: Today carries a printed ring; anything resolved grays toward the board like past dates.
Every record owns a strict end-label grid: name, category, status, age - never decorative rows.
Color enters only at hairline edges - urgency lives in a single band, never a wash.

options.risk: Residents may find it cold and unreadable; pure B/W strips away the color semantics severity needs, and strobing is an accessibility hazard we would have to engineer away.

options.label: The Civic Concourse
options.lineage: railway split-flap departure boards at rush hour
options.thesis: Every reported issue departs on the ward's split-flap board - filed, verified, assigned, resolved - flipping character by character as the city works.
options.viewport: A ruled board of live issue rows under a steel header; columns never move, only their flaps; aging rows light an amber lamp; rejected rows drop to dim red type; the map rides beside the board.
options.case: Beats the data field on both axes: every resident already reads a departure board, and the fixed-column table stays semantically honest underneath the theater.
options.risk: The flip theater must stay quiet enough for daily use - one clack per real change, never ambient motion.

options.label: The Midnight Diagram
options.lineage: metro rail maps fired as midnight-blue enamel murals
options.thesis: Your report is a route: from Reported it travels line by line through Verify and Assign until it arrives at Resolved - the city drawn as one legible promise of movement.
options.viewport: Midnight-blue enamel ground; the community map styled as a living transit diagram; each issue detail shows its route so far with interchange circles at department hand-offs.
options.case: Holds both axes against the leader - Delhi Metro resonance is enormous and wayfinding clarity is its native tongue - but loses narrowly to the concourse because forms and lists are not diagram-native.
options.risk: Dark enamel grounds fight outdoor daylight reading; the diagram must lighten for street use.

options.label: The Ward Almanac
options.viewport: A painted ward scene above a tear-off pad of the month's civic life; today takes the printed ring.
options.case: Beloved vernacular form, but a time-axis-only world cannot carry maps, triage, or forms.
options.kept: Today-ring state marking and the leaf-tear transition for resolution.

options.label: The Archive Wall
options.viewport: Reports shelved as end-labeled boxes; pulling one half out previews it; opening folds back tissue to the full report.
options.case: Retail delight, wrong institution - browsing boxes hides the urgency a city board must surface.
options.kept: The strict end-label grid and pull-half-out preview gesture.

options.label: The Diffraction Ledger
options.viewport: Quiet white records fringed by a narrow spectral band that encodes urgency at the edge.
options.case: Beautiful restraint, but pastel physics say weather app, not public accountability.
options.kept: Color confined to hairline band edges; the text field stays achromatic.
options.risk: Too ephemeral for potholes and sewage.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every civic-reporting SaaS ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects: hero headline, map screenshot, feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
